expectations.text: The speakers' dinner is excluded from the shared hospitality plan as a named population's top-up, routed to whoever owns speaker care.
expectations.evidence: "I can't draft a menu... it lives in event-speaker-experience."

expectations.text: The hotel room block is refused as a hospitality item and identified as a venue-contract term for the venue negotiation to carry.
expectations.evidence: "Not a hospitality decision... A room block is a contract term, owned by event-venue-sourcing."

expectations.text: No general-attendee lodging or travel standard is invented; the refusal is stated as a decision rather than skipped silently.
expectations.evidence: "I'm not inventing a standard."

expectations.text: Meal-line placement and queue signage are routed to the on-site experience owner rather than designed in this plan.
expectations.evidence: "Floor-plan placement and wayfinding belong to event-attendee-experience."

expectations.text: The plan refuses to stretch lunch to 75 minutes or push the afternoon talks back.
expectations.evidence: It says "I don't move or lengthen a slot" but sends the stretch to schedule design as a "change request". It adds "If you choose a buffet, [the case for pushing the afternoon back] is stronger." So it leaves the stretch open instead of refusing.

expectations.text: The needed service window is instead handed to the schedule owner as a requirement.
expectations.evidence: "Requirement handed over: a service window long enough for 400 people to be served and to eat."

expectations.text: The lunch format is chosen to fit the fixed 45-minute gap, weighing a buffet queue's length against that gap.
expectations.evidence: "Packaged meals shorten the queue... 45 minutes is workable for packaged service."

expectations.text: Dietary counts from every population fed and an expected-show-up figure are required as inputs before the format and order are fixed.
expectations.evidence: "Inputs needed before any order": expected-show-up number and counts from everyone fed.

expectations.text: The plan carries the alcohol posture and the evening decision as sections, with the evening published even if the answer is nothing organised.
expectations.evidence: "Either way, publish the decision, including 'the day ends at the last session'."

expectations.text: Each excluded item appears as an explicit ask routed to its owner, not silently dropped.
expectations.evidence: The scope table maps each of the five asks to an owner, with a numbered section for each.

expectations.text: No per-head cost or invented quantity figure appears in the plan.
expectations.evidence: "Examples at 400 people, as an upper bound only: about 510 cups in the morning and about 200 in the afternoon, before the buffer."

expectations.text: The plan is presented section by section for approval before anything is ordered.
expectations.evidence: "Nothing should be ordered until you approve each section."
